verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser has a first-party pricing page with a credit-based model available by subscription or direct purchase (hyperbrowser-docs-27). Community comments confirm that public pricing lists concurrency, browsing and data-transfer allowances (hyperbrowser-comm-1, hyperbrowser-comm-10). However, one user found the credit-to-usage mapping confusing (hyperbrowser-comm-2), which undercuts transparency, and the docs in the pack never state rate or concurrency limits directly. Missing for 10: first-party documented per-browser-hour or per-task credit rates, documented rate/concurrency limits per plan, clear credit-to-usage conversion.
